question: Which of the following semi-solid pharmaceutical forms with which a master formula can be prepared has greater occlusivity ?:
analysis: Occlusivity refers to the ability of a substance to form a barrier on the skin, preventing moisture loss. Hydrophobic ointments are known for their high occlusivity because they are oil-based and form a protective layer on the skin, reducing water evaporation. In contrast, creams, whether hydrophobic or hydrophilic, generally have less occlusivity due to their higher water content and lighter consistency. Hydrophilic ointments, while still ointments, are designed to be more water-miscible and thus less occlusive than hydrophobic ointments.
